e-493.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Natural Logarithm
e-493.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and $v',$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}=\frac{3}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=4x\, & ⟹\,v=\int 4x\,\text{d}x=2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}4x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{e}u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}v{u}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot (2{x}^{2}){|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}(2{x}^{2})\cdot \frac{3}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[2{(e)}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})-2{(1)}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{3})]-6{\int }_{1}^{e}x\text{d}x \\  & =6{e}^{2}-6(\frac{1}{2}\,{x}^{2}){|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =6{e}^{2}-3{x}^{2}{|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =6{e}^{2}-3({e}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =3{e}^{2}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

e-494.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
e-494.worked_solution:
We define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{4}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{4}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{4}⁡x(-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})-\int (-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,{log}_{4}⁡x+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}(-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula $\log_4{x}=\dfrac{\ln{x}}{\ln{4}}.$

e-3993.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
e-3993.worked_solution:
At first, it may not look like we have two factors. Actually, we do, but one of them is implicit. The trick is to write the integral as

$$
\int \ln{x}\,\textrm{d}x = \int \ln{x} \cdot 1 \cdot \textrm{d}x.
$$

 

Using this trick, we can now use integration by parts. We let

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the by-parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x+C \\  & =x(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Using integration by parts with u=ln(x) and dv=9x^2 dx gives v=3x^3 and du=dx/x. Thus the integral is 3x^3 ln(x)−∫3x^2 dx=3x^3 ln(x)−x^3+C, which is option a.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=9{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 9{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=3{x}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 9{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot 3{x}^{3}-\int 3{x}^{3}(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{x}^{3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=ln⁡x⟹u′=1xv′=9x2⟹v=∫9x2dx=3x3

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫9x2ln⁡xdx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=ln⁡x⋅3x3−∫3x3(1x)dx=3x3ln⁡x−∫3x2dx=3x3ln⁡x−x3+C, where C is an integral constant.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option a. Integration by parts gives 3x^3 ln(x)−x^3+C; differentiating yields 9x^2 ln(x). The deliberately submitted option c is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Natural Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=9{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 9{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=3{x}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 9{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot 3{x}^{3}-\int 3{x}^{3}(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{x}^{3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=ln(x) and dv=9√x dx gives the antiderivative 6x^{3/2}ln(x)−4x^{3/2}. Evaluating from 1 to e² gives (12e³−4e³)−(−4)=8e³+4.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=9\sqrt{x} & \,⟹\,v=\int 9\sqrt{x}\,dx=6{x}^{3/2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}9\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(6{x}^{3/2}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}\frac{6{x}^{3/2}}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})(6{({e}^{2})}^{3/2})-\operatorname{ln}⁡1(6(1)^{3/2})]-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}6\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =12{e}^{3}-4{x}^{3/2}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}} \\  & =12{e}^{3}-(4{({e}^{2})}^{3/2}-4(1)^{3/2}) \\  & =12{e}^{3}-4{e}^{3}+4 \\  & =8{e}^{3}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Natural Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=9\sqrt{x} & \,⟹\,v=\int 9\sqrt{x}\,dx=6{x}^{3/2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}9\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(6{x}^{3/2}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}\frac{6{x}^{3/2}}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})(6{({e}^{2})}^{3/2})-\operatorname{ln}⁡1(6(1)^{3/2})]-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}6\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =12{e}^{3}-4{x}^{3/2}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}} \\  & =12{e}^{3}-(4{({e}^{2})}^{3/2}-4(1)^{3/2}) \\  & =12{e}^{3}-4{e}^{3}+4 \\  & =8{e}^{3}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=ln(x²), du=2 dx/x, and v=7x³/3 gives (7x³/3)ln(x²)−14x³/9. At x=e³ this is 112e⁹/9, and at x=1 it is −14/9. The integral is therefore 112e⁹/9+14/9.

after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}) & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{2}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=7{x}^{2} & \,⟹\,v=\int 7{x}^{2}\,dx=\frac{7{x}^{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}7{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})(\frac{7{x}^{3}}{3}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}(\frac{7{x}^{3}}{3})(\frac{2}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\frac{7({e}^{3})^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(({e}^{3})^{2})}{3}-\frac{7(1)^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡((1)^{2})}{3}]-\frac{14}{3}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{7{e}^{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{6})}{3}-\frac{14{x}^{3}}{9}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}} \\  & =14{e}^{9}-(\frac{14{e}^{9}}{9}-\frac{14}{9}) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(126{e}^{9}-14{e}^{9}+14) \\  & =\frac{14}{9}(8{e}^{9}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

∫(x+7)ln⁡xdx=

a
x2ln⁡x2−7ln⁡x−x24−7x2+C
b
x2ln⁡x2+7xln⁡x−x24−7x+C
c
xln⁡x2+7xln⁡x−x4−7x2+C
d
xln⁡x2−7ln⁡x−x24+7x+C
e
x2ln⁡x2+7ln⁡x+x24−7x+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=ln(x) and dv=(x+7)dx gives v=x²/2+7x. The integral is (x²/2+7x)ln(x)−∫(x/2+7)dx=x²ln(x)/2+7xln(x)−x²/4−7x+C, matching option b.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=x+7\, & ⟹\,v=\int (x+7)\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+7)\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x)-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x)(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2}+7x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{1}{2}\int x\text{d}x-7\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2}+7x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-7x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

∫(x+7)ln⁡xdx=

a
x2ln⁡x2−7ln⁡x−x24−7x2+C
b
x2ln⁡x2+7xln⁡x−x24−7x+C

xln⁡x2+7xln⁡x−x4−7x2+C

x2ln⁡x2+7ln⁡x+x24−7x+C

EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=ln⁡x⟹u′=1xv′=x+7⟹v=∫(x+7)dx=x22+7x

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫(x+7)ln⁡xdx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=ln⁡x(x22+7x)−∫(x22+7x)(1x)dx=x2ln⁡x2+7xln⁡x−12∫xdx−7∫dx=x2ln⁡x2+7xln⁡x−x24−7x+C, where C is an integral constant.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Natural Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=x+7\, & ⟹\,v=\int (x+7)\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+7)\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x)-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+7x)(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2}+7x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{1}{2}\int x\text{d}x-7\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2}+7x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-7x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=ln(x) and dv=x⁻² dx gives the antiderivative −(ln(x)+1)/x. Evaluating from 1 to e⁴ gives −5e⁻⁴−(−1)=1−5e⁻⁴, matching option d.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} & \,⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,dx=-\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{4}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{4}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{4}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(-\frac{1}{x}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{4}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{4}}(-\frac{1}{x})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{4})(-\frac{1}{{e}^{4}})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)(-\frac{1}{1})]+{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{4}{{e}^{4}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-\frac{1}{x}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{4}{{e}^{4}}-(\frac{1}{{e}^{4}}-\frac{1}{1}) \\  & =1-5{e}^{-4}.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 6
?

Calculate ∫log3⁡xx3dx.

a
−2ln⁡x+14x2ln⁡3+C
b
−ln⁡x+2x2ln⁡3+C
c
ln⁡x+24x2ln⁡3+C
d
ln⁡x+12x2ln⁡3+C
e
2ln⁡x+1x2ln⁡3+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Use log₃(x)=ln(x)/ln(3). Integration by parts with u=ln(x) and dv=x⁻³ dx gives −ln(x)/(2x²)−1/(4x²). Dividing by ln(3) yields −(2ln(x)+1)/(4x²ln(3))+C, matching option a.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{3}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})-\int (-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Question 6
?

Calculate ∫log3⁡xx3dx.

a
−2ln⁡x+14x2ln⁡3+C
b
−ln⁡x+2x2ln⁡3+C
c
ln⁡x+24x2ln⁡3+C
d
ln⁡x+12x2ln⁡3+C
e
2ln⁡x+1x2ln⁡3+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=log3⁡(x)⟹u′=1xln⁡3v′=1x3⟹v=∫1x3dx=−12x2

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫log3⁡xx3dx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=log3⁡x⋅(−12x2)−∫(−12x2)(1xln⁡3)dx=−log3⁡x2x2+12ln⁡3∫1x3dx=−log3⁡x2x2−14x2ln⁡3+C=−ln⁡x2x2ln⁡3−14x2ln⁡3+C=−2ln⁡x+14x2ln⁡3+C, where C is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula log3⁡x=ln⁡xln⁡3.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{3}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})-\int (-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}=x\, & ⟹\,v=\int x\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{2}⁡(x)(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}=x\, & ⟹\,v=\int x\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{2}⁡(x)(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Question 8
?

Calculate ∫8ln⁡xx5dx.

a
 −ln⁡x+2x4+C
b
 −ln⁡x−14x4+C
c
 −2ln⁡x+14x4+C
d
 −4ln⁡x+12x4+C
e
 −2ln⁡x−3x4+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=ln(x) and dv=8x⁻⁵ dx gives v=−2x⁻⁴. Thus the integral is −2ln(x)/x⁴+2∫x⁻⁵ dx=−2ln(x)/x⁴−1/(2x⁴)+C=−(4ln(x)+1)/(2x⁴)+C, matching option d.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{8}{{x}^{5}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{8}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})-\int (-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{4}}+2\int \frac{1}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{1}{2{x}^{4}}+C \\  & =-\frac{4\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{2{x}^{4}}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Question 8
?

Calculate ∫8ln⁡xx5dx.

a
 −ln⁡x+2x4+C
b
 −ln⁡x−14x4+C
c
 −2ln⁡x+14x4+C
d
 −4ln⁡x+12x4+C
e
 −2ln⁡x−3x4+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=ln⁡x⟹u′=1xv′=8x5⟹v=∫8x5dx=−2x4

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫8ln⁡xx5dx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=ln⁡x⋅(−2x4)−∫(−2x4)(1x)dx=−2ln⁡xx4+2∫1x5dx=−2ln⁡xx4−12x4+C=−4ln⁡x+12x4+C, where C is an integral constant.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{8}{{x}^{5}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{8}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})-\int (-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{4}}+2\int \frac{1}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{1}{2{x}^{4}}+C \\  & =-\frac{4\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{2{x}^{4}}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

before.html:
Question 9
?

Calculate ∫8x3ln⁡(3x)dx.

a
 x4(ln⁡(3x)3−1)+C
b
 x2(ln⁡(3x)+13)+C
c
 x4(ln⁡(3x)−1)+C
d
 x2(2ln⁡(3x)+1)+C
e
 x4(2ln⁡(3x)−12)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=ln(3x), du=dx/x, and dv=8x³ dx gives v=2x⁴. Thus the integral is 2x⁴ln(3x)−∫2x³ dx=x⁴(2ln(3x)−1/2)+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=8{x}^{3}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 8{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x=2{x}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 8{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\cdot (2{x}^{4})-\int \frac{2{x}^{4}}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-2\int {x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-2\cdot \frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+C \\  & =2{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}+C \\  & ={x}^{4}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-\frac{1}{2})+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

a

b
 x2(ln⁡(3x)+13)+C
c

e

Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=ln⁡(3x)⟹u′=1xv′=8x3⟹v=∫8x3dx=2x4

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫8x3ln⁡(3x)dx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=ln⁡(3x)⋅(2x4)−∫2x4xdx=2x4ln⁡(3x)−2∫x3dx=2x4ln⁡(3x)−2⋅x44+C=2x4ln⁡(3x)−x42+C=x4(2ln⁡(3x)−12)+C, where C is an integral constant.

content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=8{x}^{3}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 8{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x=2{x}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 8{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\cdot (2{x}^{4})-\int \frac{2{x}^{4}}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-2\int {x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-2\cdot \frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+C \\  & =2{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}+C \\  & ={x}^{4}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-\frac{1}{2})+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{4}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{4}⁡(2x)}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{4}⁡(2x)\cdot (-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}})-\int (-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{4}⁡(2x)}{3{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{4}⁡(2x)}{3{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡4}(-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}})+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-\frac{1}{9{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C \\  & =-\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1}{9{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{4}⁡(2x)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}.$

Question 10
?

Calculate ∫log4⁡(2x)x4dx.

a
 −ln⁡(2x)+13x3ln⁡4+C
b
 −6ln⁡(2x)+12x3ln⁡4+C
c
 −ln⁡(2x)−19x3ln⁡4+C
d
 −6ln⁡(2x)−19x3ln⁡4+C
e
 −3ln⁡(2x)+19x3ln⁡4+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=log4⁡(2x)⟹u′=1xln⁡4v′=1x4⟹v=∫1x4dx=−13x3

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫log4⁡(2x)x4dx=∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx=log4⁡(2x)⋅(−13x3)−∫(−13x3)(1xln⁡4)dx=−log4⁡(2x)3x3+13ln⁡4∫1x4dx=−log4⁡(2x)3x3+13ln⁡4(−13x3)+C=−ln⁡(2x)3x3ln⁡4−19x3ln⁡4+C=−3ln⁡(2x)+19x3ln⁡4+C, where C is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula log4⁡(2x)=ln⁡(2x)ln⁡4.

content.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{4}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{4}⁡(2x)}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{4}⁡(2x)\cdot (-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}})-\int (-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{4}⁡(2x)}{3{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{4}⁡(2x)}{3{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡4}(-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}})+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-\frac{1}{9{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C \\  & =-\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1}{9{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{4}⁡(2x)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}.$

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}=\frac{3}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{3}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

u=ln⁡(x3)⟹u′=1x3⋅3x2=3xv′=1⟹v=∫dx=x

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
content.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}=\frac{3}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{3}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

decision.explanation: Change base to ln(2x+1)/ln(3), then substitute t=2x+1. The integral is [t ln(t)−t]/(2ln(3))+C. Absorbing the constant −1/(2ln(3)) into C gives option d.

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{2}{2x+1} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\int \frac{2x}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use a substitution $2x+1=u,$ thus $2x=u-1$ and $\text{d}x=\frac{\text{d}u}{2}.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\int (\frac{2x}{2x+1})\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\int \frac{u-1}{u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{1}{2}\int \,\text{d}u+\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{\text{d}u}{u}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{u}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡u}{2}+D] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{2x+1}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)}{2}+D] \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-2x+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{(2x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-2x}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=D-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}$ is an integral constant.

EXPLANATION

First, we write the integral as ∫log3⁡(2x+1)dx=∫ln⁡(2x+1)ln⁡3dx=1ln⁡3∫ln⁡(2x+1)⋅1⋅dx.

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=ln⁡(2x+1)⟹u′=22x+1v′=1⟹v=x

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫log3⁡(2x+1)dx=1ln⁡3∫ln⁡(2x+1)dx=1ln⁡3∫uv′dx=1ln⁡3[uv−∫vu′dx]=1ln⁡3[xln⁡(2x+1)−∫2x2x+1dx]

Now, we use a substitution 2x+1=u, thus 2x=u−1 and dx=du2. Hence,

∫log3⁡(2x+1)dx=1ln⁡3[xln⁡(2x+1)−∫(2x2x+1)dx]=1ln⁡3[xln⁡(2x+1)−∫u−1u⋅du2]=1ln⁡3[xln⁡(2x+1)−12∫du+12∫duu]=1ln⁡3[xln⁡(2x+1)−u2+ln⁡u2+D]=1ln⁡3[xln⁡(2x+1)−2x+12+ln⁡(2x+1)2+D]=2xln⁡(2x+1)−2x+ln⁡(2x+1)2ln⁡3+C=(2x+1)ln⁡(2x+1)−2x2ln⁡3+C,

where C=D−12ln⁡3 is an integral constant.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
content.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{2}{2x+1} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\int \frac{2x}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use a substitution $2x+1=u,$ thus $2x=u-1$ and $\text{d}x=\frac{\text{d}u}{2}.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\int (\frac{2x}{2x+1})\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\int \frac{u-1}{u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{1}{2}\int \,\text{d}u+\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{\text{d}u}{u}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{u}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡u}{2}+D] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{2x+1}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)}{2}+D] \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-2x+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{(2x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-2x}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=D-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}$ is an integral constant.

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}\operatorname{ln}⁡4x\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}\operatorname{ln}⁡4x\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int 1\cdot \,dx=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}-{\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}v{u}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\,(x){|}_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}-{\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}x(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡(4\cdot \frac{{e}^{3}}{4})\,(\frac{{e}^{3}}{4})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(4\cdot \frac{1}{4})\,(\frac{1}{4})]-{\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)-x{|}_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{e}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{e}^{3}+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(2{e}^{3}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

∫2log3⁡(x)dx=

a
2xln⁡3(ln⁡x+1)+C
b
2xln⁡3(3ln⁡x−1)+C
c
2xln⁡3(2ln⁡x−1)+C
d
2xln⁡3(ln⁡x−1)+C
e
3xln⁡2(2ln⁡x−1)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Using log₃(x)=ln(x)/ln(3), the integral is (2/ln(3))(x ln(x)−x)+C=(2x/ln(3))(ln(x)−1)+C, matching option d.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int 2{log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x=\int 2\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x=\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2{log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 1\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

∫2log3⁡(x)dx=

a
2xln⁡3(ln⁡x+1)+C
b
2xln⁡3(3ln⁡x−1)+C
c
2xln⁡3(2ln⁡x−1)+C
d

e
3xln⁡2(2ln⁡x−1)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we write the integral as ∫2log3⁡(x)dx=∫2ln⁡xln⁡3dx=2ln⁡3∫ln⁡x⋅1⋅dx.

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining u and v′, as follows:

u=ln⁡(x)⟹u′=1xv′=1⟹v=x

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫2log3⁡(x)dx=2ln⁡3∫ln⁡xdx=2ln⁡3∫uv′dx=2ln⁡3[uv−∫vu′dx]=2ln⁡3[xln⁡x−∫x⋅1xdx]=2ln⁡3[xln⁡x−∫1dx]=2xln⁡xln⁡3−2xln⁡3+C=2xln⁡3(ln⁡x−1)+C, where C is an integral constant.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
content.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int 2{log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x=\int 2\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x=\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2{log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 1\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/3}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1/3}^{e}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1/3}^{e}-{\int }_{1/3}^{e}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x){|}_{1/3}^{e}-{\int }_{1/3}^{e}x(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡(3e)-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡1-{\int }_{1/3}^{e}\,\text{d}x \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡(3e)-x{|}_{1/3}^{e}\, \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡(3e)-(e-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡3+e-e+\frac{1}{3} \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡3+\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/3}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1/3}^{e}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1/3}^{e}-{\int }_{1/3}^{e}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x){|}_{1/3}^{e}-{\int }_{1/3}^{e}x(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡(3e)-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡1-{\int }_{1/3}^{e}\,\text{d}x \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡(3e)-x{|}_{1/3}^{e}\, \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡(3e)-(e-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡3+e-e+\frac{1}{3} \\  & =e\operatorname{ln}⁡3+\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
